m.aarti.tek: Victory to you, lord of Lakṣmī; victory to you, Master, lord of Lakṣmī. Master Satyanārāyaṇa, you take away the sins of the people.
m.aarti.pad1: On the jewel-studded throne your wondrous beauty shines. Nārada waves the lamps in worship, and the bell rings out.
m.aarti.pad2: You appeared for the sake of the Kali age and gave a brāhmaṇa your darśana; taking the form of an old brāhmaṇa, you made a palace of gold.
m.aarti.pad3: You showed grace to the poor Bhīl woodcutters; there was a king, Candracūḍa, whose misfortune you took away.
m.aarti.pad4: The merchant gained his heart's wish and gave up his faith; he suffered the fruit of it, and then sang the Lord's praise.
m.aarti.pad5: For the sake of loving devotion you took on forms time after time; those who held to faith had their tasks fulfilled.
m.aarti.pad6: A king worshipped you in the forest with the cowherd boys; Hari, compassionate to the lowly, gave him the fruit his heart desired.
m.aarti.pad7: An offering of one and a quarter measures is made to you, with bananas and dried fruits; with incense, lamps and tulasī, Satyadeva is pleased.
m.aarti.pad8: Whoever sings the āratī of Śrī Satyanārāyaṇa, says Śivānanda Svāmī, gains the fruit the heart desires.
